description: I did not establish whether Kosovo notices carry CPV codes and, if so, whether the OCDS feed exposes them. Without CPV, banking/payments lots must be identified by trilingual free-text matching, which is far noisier.

Public enterprises (ndërmarrjet publike — KEK, Posta e Kosovës, Telekomi i Kosovës, regional water companies) are major buyers of cash-collection, POS and payment-acceptance services and may procure under utility rules or publish on their own sites; I did not map their individual procurement pages.
The public 'Lista e Njoftimeve' (daily list of published notices) view referenced in e-Prokurimi user documentation was not located at a confirmed public URL.

Serbian-language coverage was exercised only at the terminology level (legislation and form names). I did not confirm whether individual notice bodies for banking lots are actually published in Serbian on the platform or only in Albanian.
Contract signature notices and contract-modification/annex notices were not separately confirmed as distinct, retrievable notice types in the feed — only contract notices and award notices were.

Donor and IFI procurement inside Kosovo (EU Office/IPA, World Bank, EBRD, UNDP) for financial-sector and payment-infrastructure projects sits entirely outside the national platform; I sampled only IOM.

It is not established whether BQK is subject to Law 04/L-042 on Public Procurement or procures autonomously under its own Executive-Board rulebook, and therefore whether its tenders appear on e-Prokurimi and whether its awards are appealable to OSHP.
AQP (Central Procurement Agency) was identified but its site structure, notice format and framework-contract listings were not inspected in this run.

Other financial-sector regulators/supervisors as buyers were not covered: the Kosovo Deposit Insurance Fund (FSDK), the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-K), the Kosovo Pension Savings Trust (Trusti/KPST), the Tax Administration (ATK) and Customs — all of which buy payment, card, collection and core-financial IT systems.

No confirmed, documented API or bulk-download endpoint exists for Kosovo procurement notices or OSHP decisions. prokurimihapur.org references an API but does not document it; e-Prokurimi and OSHP expose only HTML search.
Historical depth of OSHP decisions on the official site is unverified — it is unclear how far back oshp.rks-gov.net's searchable corpus reaches versus the D+ mirror.

Vendor-side disclosure (payment-system suppliers announcing Kosovo central-bank wins in press releases, case studies or IFI-funded project documents) was not scouted, though it is often the only public trace of a central-bank infrastructure contract.

This cell is scoped to Albanian-language media only. Serbian-language Kosovo outlets (northern-municipality and Serb-community media) were deliberately not searched, so any bank/payments signal that appears only in sr within Kosovo is uncovered by this slice.

Trade/vendor-side media were not covered: regional IT and fintech trade press, vendor press-release wires, and LinkedIn/company newsrooms of payments suppliers active in Kosovo. These often announce a win before any Kosovo outlet reports it.

No archival or historical-search capability was established for these sq outlets. Kosovo news portals restructure and quietly unpublish; several older links surfaced in this run were from paths that may not persist.

Municipal-level sq media (Prizren, Gjakovë, Ferizaj, Mitrovicë local portals and radio) were not enumerated. Municipal contracting authorities are a large share of Kosovo procurement volume and their awards are often reported only locally.

All searching this run was open-web. No site-scoped searching (site:telegrafi.com kontratë bankë, site:kallxo.com bankomat) was performed, which is the technique most likely to actually surface the low-frequency contract items this cell targets.

Only Severna Mitrovica's own municipal site was confirmed at URL level; the individual official sites of Zvecan, Zubin Potok, Leposavic, Gracanica, Strpce, Klokot, Ranilug, Partes and Novo Brdo were not individually resolved in this pass.

No Serbian-language audit source was covered: Kosovo's National Audit Office (ZKA/NKR) municipal audit reports and Serbia's DRI (Drzavna revizorska institucija) reports on Kancelarija za KiM both examine contracting and banking arrangements retrospectively.

The supply side is uncovered: Serbian-language corporate registries and bank/vendor announcements (banks operating or formerly operating in Serb-majority areas - Komercijalna/NLB, Postanska stedionica, Jugobanka; Serbian payment integrators) were not enumerated.
No archival strategy was identified for Serbian-language Kosovo sources, which are unusually volatile (outlets close, municipal sites are restructured, notices are removed after award periods).
Cyrillic-script querying was under-used: most searches ran in Serbian Latin, while Serbia-side institutional sources (NBS, kim.gov.rs, DRI) publish heavily in Cyrillic.

No register specifically enumerating licensed payment institutions / e-money institutions was isolated; they appear folded into the BQK 'institucione financiare jobankare (IFJB)' category without a payments-specific view.
Serbian-language (sr) pointer coverage is thin; only one chamber source found.
No Kosovo register of registered/qualified economic operators or debarred suppliers was located (the sq query resolved to Albania).

Public enterprises (ndërmarrjet publike) and municipalities as contracting authorities were not separately enumerated in this pass, although many are banking/payments-relevant buyers (utility billing, POS collection).
ARBK's official search is an ASP.NET form-driven site and bulk collection viability is unverified; reliance on third-party mirrors introduces freshness risk.
Only three of the nine KBA member banks (Raiffeisen, ProCredit, BPB) have an identified careers/news endpoint; TEB, NLB Prishtina, BKT, Banka Ekonomike, Credins, IsBank and Ziraat are not yet mapped.
Non-bank PSPs, e-money and payment institutions licensed by BQK (and card processors/switch operators serving Kosovo) were not enumerated in this pass; only Paysera Kosova appeared incidentally.
LinkedIn — the single richest indirect channel for this cell (company announcements, role titles, employee moves) — is ToS/login restricted and cannot be scraped.
Kosovo job adverts are removed shortly after the application deadline, so hiring signals are lost unless captured within days.

Vendor/sponsor rosters of regional events that Kosovo banks attend (Balkan Payment Forum, KosICT, Balkan Fintech Association activities, ICT chamber events) are only partially mapped, and past-edition agendas were not retrieved.

No working access to web-archive infrastructure in this session: web.archive.org was blocked at the tool level, and no alternative archive service (archive.today, Common Crawl, Bing/Google cache, national web archive) was tested as a substitute.

Pre-2016 procurement history is thin. The official OCDS feed starts in March 2016; prokurimihapur.org claims coverage from 2010 but self-reports that only 14.57 percent of extracted contracts passed quality filtering and that automated gathering began only in 2018.

Serbian-language coverage of the archival layer is demonstrated only for institutional and legal documents (D+ analysis, ZKA /sr/ publications, legacy Assembly legislation). No Serbian-language notice archive, contract register, or PPRC annual report edition was found.

Framework-agreement expiry data — the highest-value predictive signal in this cell — has an identified register (AQP centralized contracts) and an identified legal basis (one to three years, plus/minus 30 percent tolerance, automatic termination on exhaustion) but no confirmed structured field-level extraction path. Consumption against the indicative value, which determines actual early termination, is not published anywhere located.

Sector targeting is unsolved for the archival layer. No banking/payments-specific view of Kosovo procurement history exists, and it was not established whether the OCDS releases carry CPV codes or another classification usable to isolate ATM, POS, card, cash-handling and core-banking procurements.

Publicly owned enterprises and the Central Bank were not covered as archival publishers in this pass. Kosovo POEs (energy, telecom, water, post) and BQK are significant buyers of payment-adjacent technology and are frequently criticised for weak procurement planning, but their own document archives were not located.

Several priority sources in this cell are JavaScript-rendered or PDF-binary and defeated the plain fetch-to-markdown approach: krpp.rks-gov.net returned only a title, and the PPRC 2022 report returned an unparsed 2.2 MB PDF.

Removed-content detection is not yet instrumented. Nothing in the sources found reveals when KRPP or a contracting authority silently deletes or edits a historical notice, and the archival value of this cell depends on catching exactly those events.

No authoritative list of Kosovo contracting authorities with their web domains was assembled — municipality slugs for kk.rks-gov.net, which authorities use own subdomains (gjakova.rks-gov.net style), and which have no site at all are all unknown.
Serbian-language Kosovo municipal sources (North Mitrovica, Zvečan, Zubin Potok, Leposavić and other Serb-majority municipalities) are entirely uncovered.

Every candidate in this slice is marked access-unverified; only one live fetch was attempted and it failed on DNS. Liveness, robots.txt posture and bot-defence behaviour are unknown across the whole cell.

Bid-opening minutes, tender dossiers and signed contract PDFs — the detail this cell exists to capture, over and above the central portal — were only confirmed at msh.rks-gov.net and bqk-kos.org. Whether municipalities publish that depth is untested.

Health-sector buyers below the ministry (SHSKUK, regional hospitals, QKUK) and the pension/social-transfer payment side of MFPT were not reached, despite being among the largest disbursement operations in the country.

The exact machine-readable endpoints for the World Bank procurement notice search and for ECEPP's country/sector-filtered notice search were not established in this pass; only the human-facing URLs were identified.

Several plausible donor actors in this cell were not searched or not resolved: Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB), Swiss SECO/SDC, Austrian ADA, Italian AICS, Luxembourg cooperation, IFAD, and the World Bank Group's Western Balkans regional digital/payments programmes; also the EU's Western Balkans Investment Framework (WBIF) and Growth Plan / Reform and Growth Facility procurement.

Albanian coverage is solid (njoftim për kontratë, njoftim për dhënie të kontratës, njoftim specifik për prokurim, ftesë për ofertë, prokurim, tenderët) but Serbian-language terminology for donor procurement in Kosovo remains largely untested against real notice text.
Donor notices are short-lived: MFK, GIZ and BQK drop PDFs that are later rotated off, and UNDB's shutdown removes a historical archive.

No mapping yet exists between donor project ids (P507881, MCC compact, EBRD operation numbers) and the implementing entities and winning suppliers that appear in Kosovo notices, so awards cannot yet be rolled up by programme or by vendor.
TED and the EU Funding & Tenders Portal are JavaScript-heavy single-page applications; naive HTML fetching will not yield notice content.
Award notices name consortium leaders, not the sub-contractors who actually deliver payment-system or card-personalisation components.
IPA III indirect-management contracts awarded by Kosovo authorities under EU rules (CFCU-type arrangements) were not mapped in this pass.
No archival/bulk historical view of Kosovo-related TED notices was established (pre-eForms TED XML, and third-party archives such as OpenTED/OpenOpps).
No primary sq- or sr-language EU-channel tender feed exists for Kosovo; local-language coverage of this cell is currently only via glossary terms and third-party aggregators.
BQK's own donor-funded award notices and the World Bank Financial Sector Development Project surfaced inside this EU-focused cell.
Two licensed Kosovo banks in the cell — ProCredit Bank Kosova and Ziraat Bank Kosova — plus Türkiye İş Bankası Kosovo branch and PriBank have no located procurement surface at all.
No source in this cell reveals who wins Kosovo bank contracts or at what value; the pipeline sees demand signals only, never awards.

Serbian-language procurement terminology yielded no Kosovo bank sources, and Turkish procurement terminology ('ihale', 'satın alma', 'tedarikçi') was not exercised against the Turkish-parent banks (TEB, BKT, Ziraat, İş Bankası) which collectively form a large share of the market.
Bank tender pages are rolling and mostly undated (BPB showed no dates at all); historical notices vanish or fall behind 'Më shumë' expanders and archive links, so backfill depth is unknown.
The most valuable technical detail sits inside downloadable PDFs (TEB RFQ/IFB/RFP packs, BPB attachments) or is released only on request to procurement mailboxes, not in the HTML notice text.

It is unconfirmed whether Kosovo job/announcement portals and print classifieds (Koha Ditore, Zëri, Bota Sot) actually republish commercial-bank 'ftesë për ofertë' notices, which would be the main fallback for banks with no tender page.

The BQK register PDF could not be parsed in this run, so the authoritative enumeration of licensed PIs, EMIs and money-transfer NBFIs (beyond UFP, Moneta and the fintechs found via press) is still incomplete.
Mobile operators' payment arms (Telekomi i Kosovës/Vala, IPKO) were only partially covered — IPKO, being privately owned, publishes no procurement and was not reached by these queries.
No sr-language sources for this cell were found; north-Kosovo payment/remittance arrangements are unrepresented.
Because private payment firms do not tender publicly, contract intelligence for this cell must come from vendor-side disclosure, which was not systematically searched.
e-Prokurimi was identified but its search interface, filters and export behaviour were not exercised, so it is unknown whether payment-keyword monitoring can be automated or needs an account.
LinkedIn company pages of vendors and their Kosovo entities were identified as likely the richest supply-side announcement channel but were not collected (search engines surface them only as stubs).

The card-switch / card-processing supply layer for Kosovo (who runs authorisation, personalisation, acquiring processing for TEB, NLB, BKT, Banka Ekonomike, BPB, PriBank, Ziraat) is entirely unmapped.

Serbian-language (sr) supply-side coverage produced zero usable sources; no Serbian-language vendor or integrator serving Kosovo institutions (incl. the parallel/north-Kosovo banking context) was identified.
Vendor job advertisements and bank IT job ads — which name the exact systems in use — were not explored, though they are a strong indirect supply-side signal.
Several high-value vendor newsroom URLs (NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, Temenos, Cacttus) are structurally inferred from vendor identity and were not fetched in this pass.
No single confirmed aggregator or dataset reliably carries Kosovo contract AWARD notices in structured form, given the zero award counts reported for the OCDS publication.

Commercial bank and PSP tenders (the buyers that matter most for a payments vendor) are private-sector RFPs largely outside public procurement portals; only press-scraping aggregators such as NjoftimePublike claim to capture them.
Serbian-language (sr) aggregator coverage of Kosovo procurement was found to be shallow and only one genuine Kosovo-scoped section was located.
IFI/donor procurement (EBRD ecepp, World Bank, KfW, EIB) covering Kosovo financial-sector and digital projects was only partially mapped in this pass.
No confirmed archive strategy exists for notices that expire and vanish from e-prokurimi before an OCDS snapshot captures them.
None of the URLs in this slice were liveness-verified, and two (Prokurimi i Hapur freshness, the PPRC OCDS API endpoint) carry specific doubt.
Watchdog output on procurement of financial services (bank account/treasury services, card acquiring, payment terminals, core-banking or payment IT) is effectively absent.
Serbian-language watchdog coverage is thin and geographically confined to the four northern municipalities; no sr-language monitoring of central-government or CBK-level contracts was found.

Business-side and think-tank watchdogs (GAP Institute, Riinvest, INDEP, Kosovo Chamber of Commerce, American Chamber of Commerce in Kosovo) were not individually verified in this pass despite plausibly publishing procurement-integrity and access-to-finance analysis.

Investigative articles and CSO PDFs are the only surviving record of many contested awards, yet several watchdog sites mix http/https and have unstable URL schemes (cohu.org / preportr.cohu.org observed).
Partisan-leaning outlets (Insajderi, Nacionale, Paparaci) supply the highest volume of single-source-award allegations but the weakest evidentiary standard.
